newsitem.title: USA: West Virginia gains 7,200 jobs in April.
newsitem.headline: West Virginia gains 7,200 jobs in April.

text.p: West Virginia's nonfarm payroll rose by 7,200 in April to 704,800, the state Bureau of Employment Programs said Tuesday.
Every major industry group except government saw job gains. The goods-producing sector saw the increase, adding 3,800 jobs, while construction added 3,200 jobs.

Since April of last year, the state has gained 14,300 jobs for a 2.1 percent growth rate. Nearly half the annual increase was in the services sector, which gained 5,800 jobs. Trade added 3,200 over the year, the bureau said.
West Virginia's unemployment rate declined to 7.5 percent in April from 7.8 percent in March and 7.7 percent a year ago, with the number of unemployed residents dropping by 1,400 to 60,300 in April.

Earnings for private sector production and nonsupervisory workers averaged $11.36 in April, up six cents from March. Hourly earnings were up 23 cents over the year. Average weekly earnings increased $5.52 in April to $403.28 and were up $11.50 from the previous April.
